C-TABLE-DIALOG-CREATION-VERIFICATION.Summary: Restore the two disabled table-dialog creation tests and make the existing row-input focus intent survive the real dialog's opening autofocus lifecycle.
C-TABLE-DIALOG-CREATION-VERIFICATION.Problem: TEST:F-001 has two explicit skipped editor component cases because shallow dialog/input stubs leave rowInput unavailable. An opt-in real Element Plus harness on main 0a72917c restores input/confirmation execution: non-default 7×5 dimensions reach createTable and the dialog closes. The strict row-focus case remains red. Current built-renderer Chromium and WebKit traces confirm row input receives focus and then the dialog focus trap moves it to the container; both engines still create a real 7×5 table. N-TABLE-DIALOG-INITIAL-FOCUS is recorded separately from the original 77 findings and linked to TEST:F-001. This draft explicitly proposes including that narrow focus repair rather than hiding it with a stub or dropping the failed expectation.

Goals.Goal: Reactivate both named component regressions with real dialog/form/numeric-input/button controls, preserving the existing opening defaults, limits, reset, cancel and confirmation behavior.
Honor the existing initial row-input focus intent after the real dialog has completed its opening autofocus work, without subsequently stealing deliberate user focus or focusing a closed dialog.
Keep confirmation routed through the existing rich-editor or Source/Split command path with the user-entered dimensions and prove browser-level table creation.

Constraints.Constraint: Keep scope within M-011's existing editor host and verification. Opening resets rows/columns to 4/3, declared numeric limits remain rows 1–30 and columns 1–20, Cancel creates nothing, and confirmation closes the dialog and dispatches the selected dimensions once.

ObservedWriteScope: runtime changes are limited to the minimal initial-focus timing repair inside the editor host src/renderer/src/components/editorWithTabs/editor.vue. Test changes are limited to tests/renderer/components/editor-coverage.test.js (restoring the two skipped cases with real-control interactions plus mutation controls) and the planned browser artifact tests/e2e/table-dialog.spec.ts. Verification bookkeeping is limited to M-011/V-M-011 scenario metadata and local semantic markup where changed. No other runtime, dialog design, dependency or infrastructure file is in scope.

Use the dialog's actual readiness/focus lifecycle for initial row focus rather than an arbitrary timeout or retry loop. A close, unmount or superseding opening invalidates stale focus work. Preserve the dialog's focus containment and normal focus restoration.

Do not move focus back to rows after the user has deliberately moved to columns or a footer button while the dialog opens. The final opening focus must be rows when no such user action supersedes it; do not satisfy the test by calling focus only before the focus trap overwrites it.

Keep normal paragraph actions, mirror/read-only safeguards, Source/Split routing, keyboard behavior, document ownership, Markdown/history/save semantics and supported table behavior unchanged. No new dialog design, dimensions policy, keyboard shortcut or persistence field.

The repaired tests use actual rendered controls and button/input interactions. Existing Muya mocking in the component suite remains an explicit boundary; browser tests must inspect the actual resulting table/model. Do not replace the row input with a fake focus method, call the confirmation handler instead of its button, remove the current strict focus expectation or alter skips/timeouts/retries/floors to pass.

Preserve the 198 already-active component cases and restore the two skipped cases. A Node-compatible import of the installed library in the test harness is permitted without changing dependencies, production bundling or global test configuration.

The additional focus finding remains separately identified and linked; approving this spec explicitly includes that bounded product repair, not a silent expansion of the original 77-record ledger. The existing sequential mode and QA/prepared-fixes priority remain in force.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No general focus manager, Element Plus upgrade, dialog/restyle work, cleanup of unrelated legacy size props, table-model/layout refactor, source-mode redesign or new permission surface.
No claim that the current failing component check is fixed, that browser shim tests establish native IPC/owner acceptance, or that a local draft delivers TEST:F-001.
No signing-boundary C-50 work, version/tag/release/signing/workflow dispatch/publication authority or rewrite of archived provenance.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Both previously skipped tests run: the registered paragraph action opens the actual dialog at 4×3, declared limits and stable row focus are verified, editing/cancel creates nothing, reopening resets values, and actual inputs set 7×5 before the real confirmation button dispatches exactly one matching createTable call and closes the dialog.

After the real opening lifecycle settles, rows retains focus unless superseded by deliberate user focus. Cancel/reopen, fast close/unmount and a user moving to columns or a footer button do not cause stale focus or focus theft. Reverting the focus repair reproduces the current strict focus failure; do not suppress the opening lifecycle to obtain a pass.

Independent controlled mutations of defaults/reset, missing creation, transposed or ignored dimensions, and omitted close are rejected by the relevant restored tests. Exact runtime bytes are restored after mutation checks; no mutant enters the candidate.

Chromium and WebKit exercise the production renderer through the actual menu-command/dialog path. Default opening, Cancel, non-default 7×5 confirmation, DOM table row/column dimensions and canonical Markdown are checked. Existing Source/Split confirmation routing retains positive coverage. Native/owner/platform limits remain explicit until verified or separately excepted.

The full editor component suite and relevant command tests pass without reducing the existing 198 active cases; no assertions, skips, retries, timeout or coverage threshold is weakened. Current pre-fix ESM import failure, strict focus failure and two-engine traces remain separately preserved as provenance.

Update M-011/V-M-011 and local semantic markup where changed, complete appropriate review/final commands and exact-candidate hosted gates, then obtain required apply/archive and collecting-train accounting before declaring delivery. No release is inferred.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The e2e test is a future implementation artifact. Preserve baseline 198 passed/2 skipped, opt-in real-control confirmation pass and strict focus failure, and production browser input→container focus traces with successful 7×5 table controls.

Use actual lifecycle and user-focus interleavings; distinguish mounted host/Muya spy proof, browser model proof and native acceptance. All owned preview/browser/test artifacts must be stopped and cleaned, preserving toolchain caches and reproducible evidence.

Assumptions.Assumption: This is a proposal, not approval to edit runtime. The current test-only candidate stays unpublished and retains its failing focus assertion until the approved change is executed.

The future plan selects the smallest existing dialog lifecycle hook and binds exact execution scopes. Spec approval permits sequential planning, not execution of an unwritten plan or integration/release.
